subject: Request: expedited evidence access and notification carveouts for forensic snapshot
messages:
From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@skylark.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Potential data exfiltration probe — request for timeline & evidence

Hi Rishi,

We observed anomalous outbound activity from a small set of customer sessions tied to our integration with Redwood (customer ID ends with -SKY). This looks like a targeted exfil attempt; we are still triaging but need to move quickly. For our DPA and internal regulators, can you confirm: 1) Redwood's incident notification window and 2) whether we can request an encrypted forensic snapshot and access to session logs?

Specifically we need: IP addresses and timestamps for the last 7 days, any KV-cache export metadata, and a forensic snapshot if available. We are working under a tight regulatory timeframe and need to agree transfer steps for cross-border data.

I attached the alert output and a short triage table (skylark-alert.txt). Please advise the Redwood liaison and next steps.

Thanks,
Alex Reed
Security Ops | Skylark Health

Attachments: skylark-alert.txt (text)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@skylark.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exfiltration probe — request for timeline & evidence

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the alert. I can confirm Redwood will follow the DPA notification obligations but we need to align on scope and transfer method before any snapshot is exported.

Immediate plan:
- We will acknowledge an incident notice to Skylark within 24 hrs (this message is the record).
- Internal triage next 12 hrs to validate scope; Ben will lead capture of session logs and IPs.
- Legal (Kim) will confirm whether any 72-hour statutory notification can be adjusted; our standard DPA §7(c) calls for notification within 72 hours of confirming an incident.

Proposed evidence handoff workflow (for discussion):
1) Initial metadata export (IPs, timestamps, user IDs) via secure attachment within 48 hrs.
2) If Skylark requests a full encrypted forensic snapshot, we propose a staged transfer: upload to a Redwood-encrypted drive and provide an ephemeral key after procurement/NDAs are in place. Transfer timeline target: snapshot available within 5 business days of request unless legal restricts export.

We may need to request a temporary carveout to the 72-hour public notification if cross-border export approvals are required; asking for a 96-hour operational window to allow coordination with subprocessors. This is a limited ask to avoid violating export rules and to ensure evidence integrity.

I've attached the internal incident evidence request we use (redwood-incident-ask.pdf). Ben — can you start pulling the logs Alex requested and add the first export bundle to the secure drive? Kim — please advise on the carveout language and quick approvals process.

Thanks,
Rishi
VP, Customer Security & Trust | Redwood Inference

Alex / Team — looping in Legal response and what we can and cannot do under our standard DPA. Short answers up front: we will prioritize Skylark's requests, but any cross-border export of customer data requires review of subprocessors and a signed limited evidence transfer agreement (LETA) and an NDA if the export contains personal data.

Key contractual points to note:
- DPA §7(c) (Notification): Redwood notifies customers "without undue delay and where feasible within 72 hours of determining an incident." That remains our starting point. Exceptions are possible but require a written escalation and sign-off from Legal + Security (we can document a 96-hour operational window for certain cross-border transfers where local law compels a hold).
- Subprocessors: any snapshot that contains data processed by subprocessors will require us to confirm subprocessors' retention and export policies before transfer. This can add time depending on jurisdiction.
- Evidence transfer: We can provide an encrypted forensic snapshot via our secure drive; transfer will be gated behind an LETA + NDA + procurement authorization. We will provide an encrypted container and ephemeral key exchange.

Action items for Skylark to expedite:
1) Execute the attached NDA/LETA (DocuSign link below) to allow snapshot export.
2) Confirm the minimal dataset you need (IPs + session meta vs. full payload). A narrower scope speeds handoff.
3) Provide point-of-contact for procurement to approve cross-border transfer costs.

DocuSign (NDA/LETA): https://app.docusign.com/rooms/EDA-2394827/secure-nda
Secure transfer path (read-only): https://drive.redwood.com/s/forensic-snapshots/enc-2037

If Skylark agrees to the LETA and a scoped dataset, we can commit to the staged timeline Rishi proposed. If you require a hard 72-hour published notice to regulators, we need to understand the regulator and legal basis — some jurisdictions mandate immediate notification and will affect our subprocessors.

Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference
